concept_model.one_line: VAE V22 looks at a photographed sumi-ink painting the way a trained critic would, but with measurement doing everything measurement can: Python measures the sheet, a model judges only what cannot be measured, three independent model readings are voted, and code turns the settled judgments into a 1-10 rating.
concept_model.audience_note: this spec serves two uses: explaining the VAE to others (read concept_model first) and operating/maintaining it (everything after)
problem: Peter Yuill paints large abstract sumi-ink works (mega-brushes, Chinese papers, ~97x180 cm), a year-long Crucible Year practice of 368+ numbered works T_001..
he wants an accurate, trackable 1-10 rating per work, comparable across the year, to see what improved and how

previous engines (V7/V10/V10C) felt 'only slightly better than a guess'; they rewarded heavy, textured, layered material load, which is Peter's baseline, not his quality: T_323 (Peter 5) scored 9 and T_326 (Peter 6) scored 10
a first V22 attempt decomposed judgment into a 14-step, per-cell evidence cascade; two blind reads of the same paintings disagreed on 30-70% of axes, so finer decomposition did not buy reliability
approach: measure first: deterministic Python on the 16-bit TIFF master measures every property that can be measured (ink masses, edges, overlaps, stroke paths, weight, unpainted voids, movement directions, edge contact) and hands those to the model as facts that outrank its own reading
judge lean: the model answers one categorical question per axis, choosing a rung on a fixed five-rung ladder, writing its observation before its choice and naming what fails the next rung up
buy consistency by ensembling: the same lean call is run three times independently and voted; disagreement is reported as unresolved, never averaged

make rarity structural: the top rung ('master') means the excellent quality held everywhere without exception plus one further property, proven by a complete survey, and it only survives if all three runs independently award it with high confidence; Python checks the survey against the measurements
keep the number out of the model: the model never sees a score; code computes the rating from the settled rungs with weights Peter can read and change
how_it_works: Step 1 (Python, zero model calls): from the TIFF, find ink (darkest 5 of 9 tonal bands), split it into elements, splatter and residue; profile every edge (crisp, soft, broken, bloom-like); find cells where passes overlap and how many tonal bands they hold; trace each stroke's path, width and endpoints; count masses and weight displacement; find held voids (paper with ink on opposite sides) and how crisp their limits are; read the dominant and opposing movement directions; record where ink meets each sheet edge and where weight sits against the sheet's centre, centre lines and edge midpoints
Step 1 output is validated against Peter's eye via colour overlays, never against a model

Step 2 (model): one prompt per painting carries the measured facts in plain cell-named English plus five views of the sheet (the photograph, a greyscale with a red 6x3 grid, a hand-picked close-up crop, an inverted view showing unpainted paper as shape, a low-pass view showing weight); the model names the sheet's parts, then classifies 13 axes
Step 2 (code): validate each run's JSON, cap any rung-4 claim whose survey contradicts a measurement, vote the three runs per axis, apply the master gate, compute the rating
Step 3 (model, later): turns the settled findings into readable critical prose in four sections plus a free response ('NEON'), forbidden to change any finding

axes_plain.A1: Material Control: did the ink's behaviour on this paper stay governed; rare = a material behaviour (a halted bleed, a contained bloom) doing structural work where loss was likeliest
axes_plain.A2: Edge Command: do edge kinds vary with structural role; rare = an edge alone carries a relationship (a crisp shared edge locks ink and void)
axes_plain.A3: Stroke Conviction: do principal strokes read as committed continuous acts; rare = a full-length stroke with visible velocity that stays sound in every phase
axes_plain.B1: Layer Architecture: do overlapping passes stay distinct with consistent depth; rare = the darkest register confined to structural positions
axes_plain.B2: Resolution: did the sheet stop where its structure was complete (no clutter in voids, unresolved ends, filling, retrace); rare = every part costs something if removed
axes_plain.C1: Void: is unpainted paper a shaped, load-bearing part of the structure; rare = void and ink lock at crisp shared junctions and the void reads as a shape in its own right
axes_plain.C2: Equilibrium: how the weight is handled; rare = balance held by opposing movements, not mass alone
axes_plain.C3: Directional Structure: what organises movement; rare = two opposing movements, each spanning a third of the sheet, unified by a shared centre, void or axis
axes_plain.C4: Frame Engagement: how the structure meets the four edges; rare = three or more edges each doing a different named job with the structure placed against the sheet
axes_plain.C5: Load-Bearing Parts: do parts beyond the primary carry load nothing else could; rare = removing a part changes a property of the primary itself
axes_plain.D1: Chance Integration: what the painting did with chance events (bloom, splatter, drip); rare = the event was made to happen there and the passage's structure depends on it
axes_plain.D2: Visual Cadence: where a unit repeats, does the sequence do something; rare = a deliberate break in the sequence that the structure uses
axes_plain.D3: Risk: how difficult was what the sheet attempted, and did it hold; rare = two or more high-difficulty acts hold and the sheet's principal relation depends on both

rung_meaning.0: structural failure (must sit in a structural position or recur)
rung_meaning.2: strong: a named quality clearly achieved, a minority
rung_meaning.3: excellent: the quality in a compound demanding form, uncommon
rung_meaning.4: master: rung 3 held everywhere without exception plus a further property; a handful across a career

concept_model.rating: rating = clip(3 + 2 x weighted mean rung, 1, 10) over resolved axes; pre-calibration weights: structural C1-C4 x2, A2 A3 B2 C5 D1 x1, A1 B1 D2 D3 x0.5; an all-competent sheet (every axis rung 1) rates 5; weights will be refit against Peter's own ratings on a 16-work calibration set

pipeline.name: deterministic measurement
pipeline.input: TIFF 16-bit master /mnt/c/cortex/images/TIFF 16-BIT/t_NNN.tif (+ 2576px analysis JPEG for field_scale/gesture topology)
pipeline.output: data/measurements/<group>/T_NNN.json, one file per group, overwrite by work_id (deterministic)

groups.segmentation: A: elements (connected ink >= 0.5 cell length, orientation-split by structure tensor), splatter attached to parent elements (per-blob then per-cluster vote), independent residue (individual + populations with width/tone/interval constancy)
groups.boundary_profile: B: per-element per-cell edge segments; trait HARD | SOFT_FEATHERED | BROKEN_RAGGED | UNCERTAIN_BLOOM_FAMILY | UNCLASSIFIED from width/fill_ratio_p10/ring_depth/frag_count; mask_reconstruction_reliable flag
groups.pass_overlap: C: candidate cells (ink density >= 0.3 or >= 2 elements) with density, darkness, tone_std, band_area_fractions (9 bands), n_bands_occupying (bands >= 15% of cell), entropy, coherence, orientation peaks; not a verdict
groups.gesture_profile: D: per element skeleton longest path, width profile, endpoint fill/fragment evidence at radii 50/100/200/300 px, likely_failed (fill@200 <= 0.30, advisory), width_turn events
groups.field_scale: E: num_masses (blur sigma 0.08*short side, threshold band<=4, >=1% area), mass displacement label CENTRED|<compass>_SLIGHT|<compass>_MARKED (<0.05 / >0.15 of half-diagonal), element_groupings
groups.voids: held voids H1..: closing of structural ink (disk r=0.2*short side) AND paper with structural ink before/after along row or column within 2r; per void cells, area_fraction, held_axes, touches_edges, perimeter_by_cell{ink_edge_px, crisp_fraction (Sobel/8 >= 0.06)}, open_perimeter_fraction, marks_inside(+cells)
groups.orientation_field: structure tensor (sigma 0.01*short side) on ~1440px luma with specks painted out by grey closing (25px); axial angles 0-180 (0 horizontal, 90 vertical, CCW, y up); dominant family = histogram peak (36 bins); opposing = peak >= 45 deg away and >= 0.35 of dominant; per-cell angle/strength; extent = share of 6 long-axis positions
groups.frame_contact: per edge N S W E: contact_fraction, runs (fractions along edge), margin_fraction; weight_centre (darkness below paper median tone) and densest_point (blur sigma 0.08) with cell and anchors within 0.05 (sheet centre, centre lines, edge midpoints)

shared.ink: Rec.709 luma quantised to 9 equal bands over 0-65535; ink = band <= 4 (darkest 5 of 9)
shared.grid: landscape 6 cols A-F x 3 rows; portrait 3 cols A-C x 6 rows; cell_at(x,y,w,h)
shared.sheet_view: deterministic/sheet.py: block-mean luma to ~1440px long side; structural_ink = ink minus components < 0.0005 of sheet

rules.title: What each rung means.
rules.text:
Every ladder has the same shape:

| Rung | Meaning | How often it occurs in a body of work |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | A structural failure | Occasional |
| 1 | Competent, well-made | Most sheets |
| 2 | Strong: a named quality clearly achieved | A minority |
| 3 | Excellent: the quality achieved in a compound, demanding form | Uncommon |
| 4 | Master: the rung 3 quality held everywhere it applies, without a single exception, plus a further property | A handful across an entire career |

Each rung above 1 names a specific condition. A sheet reaches it when the condition is visibly met and not otherwise.

rules.title: Rung 4 requires a complete survey.
rules.text: To record rung 4, fill `master_survey`: list every place the rung's condition applies (every structural edge, every part, every overlap, as the axis names), and state for each that the condition holds there. One place where it does not hold, or one place the images cannot resolve at their resolution, means the axis is rung 3. Rung 4 is never recorded at `MODERATE` or `LOW` confidence.

rules.title: Failure rungs are structural.
rules.text: A rung 0 fault must sit in a structural position (on the primary, at the principal void, at a pivot) or recur in two separate regions. A single slip in a peripheral passage is recorded in the `decision_note` and does not decide the axis, except at rung 4, where any exception counts.

rules.title: Observe, then classify.
rules.text: Write the `observation` first, in plain descriptive words with cells named and no ladder vocabulary. Then choose the `value`. The value follows from the observation as written. If it does not, change the value, never the observation.

rules.title: Check your rung and the one above it.
rules.text: In `rung_check`, state the chosen value's condition and the observation that meets it. Then state the next rung's condition and the specific thing on the sheet that fails it. A reason names a cell, a part, or a missing property. "Being conservative" is not a reason. If the sheet meets the next rung's condition, the next rung is the answer.

rules.title: Compound conditions need one connected story.
rules.text: Where a rung names two properties, they must depend on each other in the same place. A property that would hold anyway, or that follows from a part simply being large, does not count.

rules.title: The strongest instance decides
rules.text: rungs 1 to 3. Where an axis looks at several parts or events, the value comes from the strongest one that meets a rung. Weak or incidental instances never pull a strong one down below rung 3. Rung 4 is the exception: it is a claim about every instance.

rules.title: One observation may serve several axes
rules.text: when each axis tests a different property of it.

rules.title: Evaluate what is present.
rules.text: One gesture or many, the same ladders apply. `NOT_PRESENT` means the thing the axis measures is absent from this sheet. `NOT_ESTABLISHED` means the images do not resolve it. Both are decided before the ladder and neither is a rung.

rules.title: Confidence.
rules.text: Each axis carries `HIGH`, `MODERATE` or `LOW`. Below `HIGH`, write a `decision_note`: the value you did not choose and the one observation that decided it. Confidence never changes which value the evidence supports.

definitions.Structural position: Within the primary part, at the limit of the principal void, or at a place where two movements meet.
definitions.Structural edge: The primary's outline, every limit of a held void, and every junction.
definitions.Held: A void is held when ink lies on two opposite sides of it and its limit is findable against each.
definitions.Junction: Where a part's edge meets another part or a held void. An edge against open, unheld paper is not a junction. Two junctions are distinct only if, along the boundary between them, there is a stretch where the edge is not shared. One continuous shared edge is one junction however many cells it crosses.
definitions.Dry brush: Gaps running parallel to the stroke's travel. It is a technique, not a broken edge. Gaps that are irregular or cross the direction of travel are broken.
definitions.Movement: A direction that governs a set of passes: a sweep, a rotation, a fan radiating from a centre, a stack.
definitions.Full length: Contiguous cells reaching both the first and the last third of the sheet's long axis.
definitions.Heavy demand: A cell carrying three or more overlapping passes, wet meeting wet where neither edge survives, or a rewetted area shown by a ring at its edge.

counterfactual_protocol.C1: Name the target (a part, a void or an event) and its cells. State what you expect to change if it were removed, or, for a void, filled with the neighbouring tone, or, where an axis says so, shifted by one cell. Target and prediction come before the result.
counterfactual_protocol.C2: If the result does not support the rung you expected, that is the result. Do not switch target or prediction because the first came back unhelpful.
counterfactual_protocol.C3: as a present-tense claim about two named things at named cells. *"Filling V1 in C2–D3 merges P1 and P2 into one mass and P2's rotation no longer reads against P1's"* is grounded. *"Filling it would weaken the composition"* is not.

A1.title: MATERIAL CONTROL
A1.question: Did the ink's behaviour on this paper stay governed?

ladder.condition: In a structural position or in two separate regions: migration runs past any limit the mark could have had, or overlapping passes collapse into a flat tone with neither pass identifiable
Ink behaves as this paper, climate and load predict; no structural loss

`GOVERNED`, and a material behaviour itself forms an edge or shape the structure uses, named: a bleed halted at a findable limit that bounds a void, a bloom contained by dry passes, a translucent overlap that makes the tone a junction depends on
`MATERIAL_SHAPES`, and that same behaviour sits in a cell of heavy demand, where loss was likeliest

`MATERIAL_SHAPES_UNDER_LOAD`, and every heavy-demand cell on the sheet stays governed and legible under `crop`, and two different material behaviours each do named structural work in separate regions. Survey: every heavy-demand cell, including every cell the overlap facts mark heavy.

notes: Record `demand`: `LIGHT`, `MODERATE` (two overlapping passes, or a pooled deposit) or `HEAVY` (as defined).

A2.title: EDGE COMMAND
A2.question: Do the edges vary, and does the variation follow the structure?

ladder.condition: Bled or broken edges run along a structural edge
Edges keep a findable limit where it matters; one kind dominates, or kinds vary without following anything

Two or more kinds are used, and the kind changes where the structural role changes, at two named places (for example, crisp at the void, dry brush at a leading terminal, soft where one pass sinks behind another)

`EDGES_DIFFERENTIATED`, and an edge alone carries a relationship: a crisp shared edge makes ink and void lock together at a junction, or a softened edge alone sets one pass behind another where their tones are the same

`EDGE_CARRIES`, and every structural edge on the sheet has the kind its role calls for with no exception under `crop`, and edge alone carries at least two separate relationships in different regions. Survey: every structural edge.

notes: Edge kinds: crisp, soft (feathered to a findable limit), dry brush, bled (no findable limit), broken.

A3.title: STROKE CONVICTION
A3.question: Do the principal strokes read as committed, continuous acts?
A3.uses_facts: largest deposits, stroke endpoint hints, width vs turn

ladder.condition: A failure signature in `P1`, or in two other principal strokes
Principal strokes proceed without failure signatures

`SOUND`, and a principal stroke carries its direction through a change without breaking: a turn with a continuous tapered profile, or a run from saturated to dry brush with the gaps parallel to travel
`COMMITTED`, and that stroke spans the full length with visible velocity (dry-brush streaking, splatter trailing its path), while every phase of it inside the sheet stays sound

`SPEED_WITHOUT_HASTE`, and every stroke on the sheet is free of every failure signature under `crop`, each principal stroke's width changes only where pressure or direction visibly changes, and at least one principal stroke has both its entry and its terminal inside the sheet, both resolved. Survey: every stroke that is a part.

notes: Failure signatures: a fuzzy or dragging start; a hesitation bulge or dot; low-velocity drag; an unmotivated break or tremor; a hollow or twisted turn; an abrupt stop with no exit direction; a premature fade; a doubled or offset corrective retrace. ## HOW TO CLASSIFY

**1. What each rung means.** Every ladder has the same shape:

| Rung | Meaning | How often it occurs in a body of work |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | A structural failure | Occasional |
| 1 | Competent, well-made | Most sheets |
| 2 | Strong: a named quality clearly achieved | A minority |
| 3 | Excellent: the quality achieved in a compound, demanding form | Uncommon |
| 4 | Master: the rung 3 quality held everywhere it applies, without a single exception, plus a further property | A handful across an entire career |

Each rung above 1 names a specific condition. A sheet reaches it when the condition is visibly met and not otherwise.

**2. Rung 4 requires a complete survey.** To record rung 4, fill `master_survey`: list every place the rung's condition applies (every structural edge, every part, every overlap, as the axis names), and state for each that the condition holds there. One place where it does not hold, or one place the images cannot resolve at their resolution, means the axis is rung 3. Rung 4 is never recorded at `MODERATE` or `LOW` confidence.

**3. Failure rungs are structural.** A rung 0 fault must sit in a structural position (on the primary, at the principal void, at a pivot) or recur in two separate regions. **4. Observe, then classify.** Write the `observation` first, in plain descriptive words with cells named and no ladder vocabulary. Then choose the `value`. The value follows from the observation as written. If it does not, change the value, never the observation.

**5. Check your rung and the one above it.** In `rung_check`, state the chosen value's condition and the observation that meets it. **8. One observation may serve several axes** when each axis tests a different property of it.

**9. Evaluate what is present.** One gesture or many, the same ladders apply. `NOT_PRESENT` means the thing the axis measures is absent from this sheet. `NOT_ESTABLISHED` means the images do not resolve it. Both are decided before the ladder and neither is a rung.

Record `geometry`: `RADIAL`, `ARC`, `ROTATIONAL`, `LINEAR`, `STACKED`, `MASSED` or `SCATTERED`.

## DEFINITIONS

**Structural position.** Within the primary part, at the limit of the principal void, or at a place where two movements meet.

**Structural edge.** The primary's outline, every limit of a held void, and every junction.

**Held.** A void is held when ink lies on two opposite sides of it and its limit is findable against each.

**Junction.** Where a part's edge meets another part or a held void. An edge against open, unheld paper is not a junction. **Dry brush.** Gaps running parallel to the stroke's travel. It is a technique, not a broken edge. Gaps that are irregular or cross the direction of travel are broken.

**Movement.** A direction that governs a set of passes: a sweep, a rotation, a fan radiating from a centre, a stack.

**Full length.** Contiguous cells reaching both the first and the last third of the sheet's long axis.

**Heavy demand.** A cell carrying three or more overlapping passes, wet meeting wet where neither edge survives, or a rewetted area shown by a ring at its edge.

### C3. DIRECTIONAL STRUCTURE
**Question:** What organises movement across the sheet?
*Uses: masses at field scale, movement directions. Images: `bw`, `lowpass`.*

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `SCATTERED` | Directions conflict with no locatable relation between them, and the masses do not read as one field |
| 1 | `SINGLE_MOVEMENT` | One movement governs; any others are incidental |
| 2 | `WITH_COUNTER` | A second movement runs against the first and stands in a named relation to it: meeting it at a pivot, bounded by it, or answering it across a void |
| 3 | `OPPOSED_AND_UNIFIED` | Two opposing movements each span at least a third of the long axis, and they share a named centre, void or axis of symmetry that makes the sheet read as one image |
| 4 | `ORCHESTRATED` | `OPPOSED_AND_UNIFIED`, and every part on the sheet aligns with, counters, or resolves one of the two movements, with none incidental, and the place where the movements meet is itself resolved cleanly, with no collision, mud or blur. Survey: every part, each with its role. |

On an `ALL_OVER` sheet, a single movement is the field's macro-rhythm (a loop, a drift, a pulse across the whole). If none exists, the value is `SCATTERED`.

### C4. FRAME ENGAGEMENT
**Question:** How does the structure meet the sheet's four edges?
*Uses: frame contact. Images: `bw`, `lowpass`.*

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `TRAPPED` | The principal part floats with no relation to any edge, or is clipped by an edge in a way that cuts off its own structure (a centre, a turn or a void lost off the sheet) |
| 1 | `CONTAINED_OR_CONTINUING` | The structure sits within margins, or runs off the edges as continuation |
| 2 | `EDGE_ACTIVE` | One named edge relation does structural work: a movement exits and implies its continuation; a part stops just short of an edge and compresses the space there; a channel or axis runs parallel to an edge; or the structure's centre or hub sits on an edge midpoint, the centre line or the sheet's centre. A placement on its own reaches this rung and no higher. |
| 3 | `EDGES_COMPOSED` | Three or more edges each do a different named job (for example: exit and continuation, compression, alignment, release into open paper), and the structure's centre, hub or axis is placed in named relation to the sheet |
| 4 | `FRAME_INEVITABLE` | `EDGES_COMPOSED` on all four edges, and shifting the whole structure one cell in any direction **(C)** breaks a named relation at an edge: every edge relation is exact. Survey: all four edges, and all four shift tests. |

### C5. LOAD-BEARING PARTS
**Question:** Do the parts beyond the primary carry load that nothing else could?
*Images: `bw`, `lowpass`.*

Test the ink parts other than `P1`, up to three (every part at rung 4). For each, run **(C)** on its removal. Where removal costs something, name the closest substitute still present (including `P1`) and run **(C)** again: could it carry that load from where it is? State why it can or cannot, by position, extent or kind.

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `REDUNDANT` | Every tested part can be removed at no named cost |
| 1 | `SUPPORTING` | A tested part carries load, but a named substitute could carry it |
| 2 | `NECESSARY` | A tested part carries load that no remaining part could carry |
| 3 | `RECIPROCAL` | `NECESSARY`, and removing that part changes a named property of `P1` itself (its direction reads differently, a limit loses definition, or its weight goes unanswered), not only the sheet around it |
| 4 | `INTERDEPENDENT` | Every ink part and `V1` is necessary, and at least two parts other than `P1` are reciprocal with it, each through a different property. Survey: every part and `V1`, each with its own test. |

`NOT_PRESENT` if the sheet has only one ink part.

### DOMAIN D: CHANCE, RHYTHM AND RISK

### D1. CHANCE INTEGRATION
**Question:** Where chance entered (bloom, backrun, splatter, drip, run), what did the painting do with it?
*Uses: splatter populations, edge segments. Images: `analysis`, `crop`, `bw`.*

A splatter population counts as one event. Events that affect each other count as one. Classify the strongest.

Moving above `ACCEPTED` needs an `evidence_route`: contained by adjacent dry passes (`CONTAINED_BY_DRY_PASSES`); the same effect repeated elsewhere (`REPEATED_ELSEWHERE`); a limit too precise to be coincidental on this paper (`PRECISE_LIMIT`); or a part's later continuation visibly adjusting to the event (`CONTINUATION_ADJUSTS`). The event's own edge kind is not a route by itself.

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `DISRUPTIVE` | The event breaks a structural edge or litters a held void |
| 1 | `ACCEPTED` | The event stands, neither disrupting the structure nor developed by it |
| 2 | `INCORPORATED` | A part visibly relates to the event, by a named route |
| 3 | `GENERATED` | Placement, extent and relation to bounding structure show the event was made to happen there, by a named route |
| 4 | `EXPLOITED` | `GENERATED`, and the passage's structure depends on the material behaviour: removing the event **(C)** removes the passage's structure, not its decoration, and every other chance event on the sheet is at least `INCORPORATED`. Survey: every chance event. |

`NOT_PRESENT` if no chance event is visible. `evidence_route` is `NONE` at rungs 0 and 1.

### D2. VISUAL CADENCE
**Question:** Where a unit repeats (spokes, stacked passes, parallel strokes), does the sequence do something?
*Uses: residue populations. Images: `bw`, `lowpass`.*

A repeated unit is two or more parts or passes made the same way. Splatter is not a repeated unit unless it is placed as a sequence. Where `known_facts` gives a repeated population's width/tone/interval constancy, treat a `false` there as confirmation a measured property varies, not proof alone that the variation is purposeful. The image must still show it stepping with a named change.

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `REPEATED` | A repeated unit exists |
| 2 | `VARIED_WITH_PURPOSE` | Interval, tone, width or length changes along the sequence in step with a named change elsewhere: spokes lengthen toward a counterweight, tone darkens toward a hub |
| 3 | `SYNCOPATED` | `VARIED_WITH_PURPOSE`, and the sequence contains a deliberate break (a missing unit, a gap, a unit out of phase) that the structure uses, named **(C)** |
| 4 | `CADENCE_MASTERED` | `SYNCOPATED`, and every unit in the sequence follows the named change except the deliberate break, and the sequence spans the full length. Survey: every unit, in order. |

`NOT_PRESENT` if nothing repeats. There is no rung 0: steady repetition is not a fault.

### D3. RISK
**Question:** How difficult was what this sheet attempted, and did it hold?
*Images: all.*

High-difficulty acts (closed list):
- `FULL_LENGTH_STROKE`: one continuous stroke across the full length;
- `CLEAN_VOID_AMID_WET`: a crisp-edged void kept clean while wet passes surround it;
- `WET_INTO_WET_AT_STRUCTURAL_EDGE`: wet meeting wet at a structural edge that stays governed;
- `OPPOSED_MOVEMENTS_WITHOUT_MUD`: two opposing movements built on one sheet without collision or mud;
- `LEGIBLE_HEAVY_DEMAND_CELL`: a heavy-demand cell whose passes stay legible.

| Rung | Value | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `FAILED_RISK` | A high-difficulty act was attempted and visibly failed in a structural position |
| 1 | `WITHIN_REACH` | No high-difficulty act, or one that the structure does not depend on |
| 2 | `RISK_HELD` | A named high-difficulty act holds, and the structure depends on it **(C)** |
| 3 | `RISK_IS_STRUCTURE` | Two or more high-difficulty acts hold, and the sheet's principal relation (its void, its opposition or its balance) depends on both |
| 4 | `MASTER_RISK` | Three or more different high-difficulty acts hold with no failure anywhere under `crop`, and the structure depends on each **(C)**. Survey: every act attempted on the sheet, held or not. |

---

## OUTPUT

Emit one JSON object, and nothing else, that validates against the supplied schema:

- `work_id`
- `parts`: `{tag, kind, cells}` for each part
- `composition_mode`, `geometry`
- `fact_conflicts`: `{fact, seen, cells}` for each place your reading seemed to contradict a known fact, or `[]`
- `axes`: one object per axis, keyed `A1` to `D3`:
  - `observation`: one to three sentences, cells named, descriptive words only, written before the value
  - `value`: a value from the ladder, or `NOT_PRESENT` where the axis offers it, or `NOT_ESTABLISHED` on any axis
  - `rung_check`: the chosen value's condition and what meets it; the next rung's condition and what fails it (omit at rung 4)
  - `confidence`, with `decision_note` below `HIGH`
  - `counterfactual`: `{target, cells, predicted, result}` for each **(C)** test the value relies on
  - `master_survey`: at rung 4 only, `{place, cells, holds, note}` for every surveyed place; on C4, add `edge` (`N`, `S`, `E` or `W`) to each edge's entry
  - `demand` (A1); `markers` as `{kind, cells}` (B2); `evidence_route` (D1, `NONE` at rungs 0 and 1); `acts` as `{act, cells, held}` (D3)

Nothing follows the object.

# PART ONE — THE READ

Four sections, in this order. Each takes its axes' findings and says, in
plain critical language, what actually happened and why it matters to
the painting as a whole — not a list of translated labels, a piece of
writing that happens to be fully grounded in them.

Word ceiling per section: about 150 words. Under is always fine.
Padding to reach it is not.

## MATERIAL & MARK-MAKING
*Axes: A1 Material Control, A2 Edge Command, A3 Stroke Conviction*

What actually happened where brush met paper. Containment or collapse,
control at the edges, whether the mark's own body holds together,
whether the stroke's phases — landing, travel, turn, exit — read as
sound or as failure. This is the most physically specific section: name
the actual mechanism, not a verdict about it.

## LAYERING & RESOLUTION
*Axes: B1 Layer Architecture, B2 Resolution*

How the passes stack, whether depth reads consistently and the darks sit
where the structure needs them, and whether the sheet stopped where its
structure was complete. If a closure failure is present, name what it
looks like, at its location.

## SPACE & STRUCTURE
*Axes: C1 Void, C2 Equilibrium, C3 Directional Structure, C4 Frame Engagement, C5 Load-Bearing Parts*

How the composition holds together as a whole, including the unpainted
paper and the sheet's own edges. Where the weight sits
and what answers it, how far the primary gesture's authority actually
reaches, whether the sheet reads as one field or several unrelated
ones, and — this is the load-bearing fact of the section — which
elements are actually necessary and which could be removed at no real
cost. This section should give a reader the clearest sense of the
painting's actual architecture, not just a list of five separate
findings.

## CHANCE, RHYTHM & RISK
*Axes: D1 Chance Integration, D2 Visual Cadence, D3 Risk*

How the accidental was handled, if anything accidental happened at all:
name the specific event and what was done with it (accepted, built on,
or left to sit uncontrolled). Whether a repeated unit does anything. How
much the sheet attempted, and whether it held.

deterministic/bands.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic tonal-band-cell extraction, computed directly from a painting's TIFF master at native 16-bit precision -- no model call, no posterized-JPEG intermediate. defs.rec709_luma16: Rec.709 luma from a 16-bit-per-channel RGB array, in the same 0-65535 range as the input.

deterministic/boundary_profile.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic boundary/edge-profile computation (Group B), computed directly from a painting's TIFF master -- no model call. defs._dense_contour: Full-resolution boundary polygon (row, col), NOT simplified -- see module docstring for why Group A's own `contour_xy` (60-point capped, tolerance=2.0) is unusable for this module's purpose.
defs._resample_uniform: Points at roughly uniform arc-length spacing along a closed polyline, by linear interpolation -- so `_curvature_roughness`'s windowed statistics aren't skewed by the raw contour's uneven native point density.
defs._curvature_roughness: High-frequency turning-angle energy along the boundary -- a general edge-texture number, kept for completeness/future use, but NOT what discriminates BROKEN_RAGGED (see module docstring).
defs._sample_profile: Perpendicular luminance profile at one boundary point, oriented OUTWARD (flips `normal` if it initially points into the mask). Returns (offsets, profile, outward_normal).
defs._local_feibai: Feibai ('flying white' -- Pete, 2026-09-17): dry-brush strokes show literal gaps WITHIN the stroke body, not a rough traced edge -- see module docstring for why this replaced curvature-roughness as the BROKEN_RAGGED signal. Samples a band biased inward from the boundary point (so it measures whether the stroke's own interior is actually solid there, not the paper side, which is expected to be empty). Returns (fill_ratio, fragment_count) within that band, read directly off the full-canvas ink mask, not the element's own (possibly orientation-split, possibly unreliable) reconstructed mask -- paper showing through inside the nominal footprint is real regardless of which element the surrounding ink was assigned to.
defs._classify: See module docstring's VALIDATION METHOD section for exactly where these thresholds and their ordering come from. Order matters: the bloom-family check runs first because it's the most specific signature (both a real ring/bump AND real fragmentation at once); BROKEN_RAGGED next because low fill_ratio is a strong, singular signal; HARD/SOFT_FEATHERED last since it's the default read when nothing more specific fired. `width_threshold_px` is HARD_SOFT_WIDTH_FRACTION_THRESHOLD already converted to this painting's own pixel scale by the caller -- see that constant's own comment for why this one (unlike ring_depth/fill_ratio/frag_count) needs the conversion.
defs.compute_boundary_segments: Public entry point -- takes exactly what Group A's `segment_ink` reports for one element (`Blob.bbox`, `.centroid_xy`, `.pixel_area`) plus the element's own `tag`, reconstructs its mask from the TIFF, and returns one `BoundarySegment` per grid cell the boundary passes through (the same per-cell grouping this module's own validation used against the model's ground truth -- see module docstring).

defs.reconstruct_element_mask: Rebuild one element's local boolean mask from Group A's own reported `bbox` (x0, x1, y0, y1) and `centroid_xy`, by re-running connected-component labeling on just that crop of the already- computed full-canvas ink mask (cheap -- a bbox crop is at most a few megapixels, versus 20-30 million for the whole canvas) and picking whichever labeled component CONTAINS the reported centroid.

deterministic/field_scale.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic field-scale/composition computation (Group E), computed directly from a painting's TIFF master and its pre-made analysis JPEG -- no model call. See module docstring's VALIDATION for why this parameter, checked directly rather than assumed. defs.compute_field_scale: Public entry point. `num_masses` is computed from the pre-made analysis JPEG (matching `gesture_profile.py`'s own use of that asset for cheap, properly-antialiased downsampled work -- blur-then- threshold needs no more precision than that, and this avoids loading the full 16-bit TIFF twice for what's fundamentally a coarse question). deterministic/gesture_profile.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic gesture/skeleton computation (Group D), computed directly from a painting's TIFF master -- no model call. Feeds part of Step 4 of `master_evidence_prompt.md` (per-element Entry/Body/ Transition/Terminal phase judgments, modulation, depletion -- Axis 4) and half of Axis 10's directional accounting.

defs._trace_longest_path: Longest shortest-path between any two skeleton pixels (the stroke's primary gesture path, ignoring minor branches), via the double-BFS tree-diameter trick -- see module docstring's design failure #1 for why not naive multi-endpoint pure-Python BFS.
defs._local_fill_ratio: Fraction of a square window (side `2*radius_px`) centered at (gy, gx) that's ink, plus how many separate connected ink fragments it contains -- read directly off the full-canvas ink mask. See module docstring's FINDING for why this, not width-profile shape, is what actually separates a clean landing/stop from a fuzzy/ dissolving one.
defs.compute_gesture_profile: Public entry point -- takes exactly what Group A's `segment_ink` reports for one element (`Blob.bbox`, `.centroid_xy`, `.pixel_area`) plus the element's own `tag`, and returns the traced gesture path's endpoints (with evidence) and width profile. Returns None if the element is too small to meaningfully skeletonize (fewer than 20 skeleton pixels in the small-resolution mask), or if no analysis JPEG exists for this work_id.

deterministic/grid_geometry.py.doc: Pixel-space grid-cell boundary computation, shared by every Tier 1 module that needs to aggregate pixel data per grid cell. Matches the pipeline's own grid convention (see /mnt/c/cortex/cy_pipeline/make_posterized.py's draw_grid()): landscape (width >= height) sheets get 6 columns (A-F) x 3 rows (1-3); portrait sheets get 3 columns (A-C) x 6 rows (1-6).

defs.cell_at: Grid label of the cell containing pixel (x, y), same convention as cell_grid.

deterministic/orientation_field.py.doc: Orientation field: which directions organise the ink, from a structure tensor on the downsampled sheet. Grounds C3 (single movement / with counter / opposed) and C2's "balance through opposing movements".

deterministic/pass_overlap.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic pass-overlap candidate detection (Group C, part 1), computed directly from a painting's TIFF master -- no model call. Feeds part of Step 6 of `master_evidence_prompt.md` ("find every cell where two or more ink passes visibly overlap... do the passes remain individually legible, fuse together, or not actually overlap on closer look"), which in turn feeds Axis 13's `pass_legibility` input.

defs.find_pass_overlap_candidates: `element_cells` is `{element_tag: [cell, ...]}` -- pass Group A's `segment_ink(work_id).elements` mapped to `{e.tag: e.cells}` if available; omit to skip the multi-element overlap signal entirely (still produces density/band/orientation evidence for every sufficiently-inked cell).

deterministic/segmentation.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic element/residue segmentation, computed directly from a painting's TIFF master at native 16-bit precision -- no model call. Replaces Step 1 of `master_evidence_prompt.md`'s current job of having the model visually find every distinct ink deposit and tag it by eye: this module finds every ink deposit via connected-component analysis on a thresholded ink mask, splits any mass containing more than one distinct gestural direction (see ORIENTATION_* constants below), and assigns tags by real computed size, not a human's estimate of size order.

defs._blob_cells: Cells this blob's actual mask (not just its bounding box) occupies above MIN_CELL_OVERLAP_PIXELS. Always returns at least one cell (the single best-overlapping one) even if none clear that threshold -- checked directly against real T_119 data: at MIN_CELL_OVERLAP_PIXELS=20, 58% of genuine small residue marks (drips, splatter) overlap no cell enough to register at all, which would make every one of them an unlocatable blob rather than a small mark that's still somewhere specific on the sheet. A blob is only truly cell-less if its mask is empty, which shouldn't reach this function at all (NOISE_FLOOR_PIXELS is filtered before here).
defs._contour_for: Simplified boundary polygon in global pixel coords, from a mask already cropped to `bbox` (min_row, min_col, max_row, max_col) -- see _blob_cells' docstring for why local, not full-canvas.
defs._orientation_field: Structure-tensor local orientation (radians, from the vertical axis, matching skimage's own convention -- see Blob.orientation_deg) and coherence (0..1, how confidently a single direction dominates at that pixel) at the given window size.
defs._find_angle_peaks: Real local maxima of a weighted circular histogram of doubled angles (mod 2*pi), smoothed, kept only if their PROMINENCE (height above their own surrounding valley, not absolute height -- see this module's SHIPPED/KNOWN LIMITATION comment above for why prominence, not height) clears PEAK_MIN_PROMINENCE_FRACTION of the total weight. Returns peak centers in the same doubled-angle space. Empty if there's no confident data at all.
defs._circular_distance: Distance from each angle in `a` to `peak`, both mod 2*pi, on the circle (never more than pi).
defs._split_by_orientation: Split one connected ink blob into sub-masks by dominant local direction, per this module's ORIENTATION_*/HISTOGRAM_*/PEAK_* constants (see the block comment above them for why this shape of algorithm, and what was tried and rejected first). `mask` is a boolean array local to the blob's own bounding box (not the full image). Returns a list of boolean sub-masks covering `mask`'s True pixels between them -- a single-entry list if the blob has only one dominant direction, i.e. this is a safe no-op for an ordinary single-gesture element.
defs._frozen_region: The six region properties this module reads, evaluated now. A regionprops region from a full-canvas label image keeps that image (int64, ~150 MB here) alive for as long as the region lives; with 10+ orientation-split sub-blobs that was the 2026-09-23 memory-cap failure on T_135/T_136/T_138 (+0.17 GB per kept sub-blob).
defs._blob_element_distances: {id(region): {element tag: min distance from any of the blob's pixels to that element}}, tags in element order. Both attachment passes need only these per-blob minima, so each element's full-canvas distance field is built, read and dropped one at a time. Holding one float64 field per element at once was the 2026-09-23 memory-cap failure on multi-element and 25 MP+ sheets (T_215, T_302, T_324, T_326, T_327: six fields alone took T_302 from 1.8 to 3.0 GB).
defs._attach_by_proximity: Per-BLOB attachment pass: a small blob within `threshold_px` (mask-to-mask, not centroid-to-centroid -- centroid distance is misleading against a long stroke) of a real element is that element's splatter -- see the ATTACHMENT_* block comment above for why this exists (T_119's 1108-blob mega-population). Blobs with no element nearby fall through to `isolated`, which is only ever clustered among ITSELF (see `_cluster_small_blobs`) -- never every small blob in the painting at once, which would let dense splatter near one element transitively drag in blobs from anywhere else on the canvas (real bug, found 2026-09-17 by testing exactly that: a single first-pass attempt at clustering-before-attachment collapsed T_219's entire 3405-blob residue field into one cluster).
defs._cluster_small_blobs: Cluster a set of small blobs into spatial groups by real pixel distance between centroids, deliberately NOT by the 6x3/3x6 cell grid. That grid exists only so a human/model can name a location in the schema's own vocabulary ("B2"); it has nothing to do with how far apart two marks actually are, and using it for a clustering decision was a real bug: with only 18 cells total, transitive cell-adjacency chains almost any two blobs together eventually (checked directly on T_119: all 1108 candidate blobs merged into one "population" spanning nearly the whole sheet). Cells are computed per blob only for the final report (via `_blob_cells`, already scale-appropriate for that purpose), never for this decision.
defs._reattach_clusters: Second attachment pass, at CLUSTER granularity -- real bug fixed 2026-09-17, found by Pete's direct visual check against T_219: three of its four residue populations (P2, P3, P4) were, by his own read of the actual painting, real splatter trailing from M1 or M2, not independent events. `_attach_by_proximity`'s tight per-blob threshold had already caught each cluster's nearest members as splatter in the first pass; what was left in each cluster missed that tight threshold individually even though the group as a whole is still plainly trailing from the same element -- a physically continuous trail shouldn't be split down the middle by where a per-blob cutoff happens to fall.
defs._finalize_residue: Turn already-formed clusters that survived both attachment passes independent (see `_cluster_small_blobs` / `_reattach_clusters`) into the final individual-vs-population report. A small cluster (at or below POPULATION_MIN_COUNT) is reported as individually-tagged blobs; a larger one is collapsed into one PopulationSummary.

defs._gaps_along_rows: Distance to the nearest ink pixel before and after each pixel along axis 1 (inf if none).
defs.enclosed_paper: Paper filled by a morphological closing of the ink with a disk of radius_px: gaps between ink masses narrower than about 2 * radius_px. Done with distance transforms so the cost does not grow with the radius. CONCEPT.one_line: VAE V22 looks at a photographed sumi-ink painting the way a trained critic would, but with measurement doing everything measurement can: Python measures the sheet, a model judges only what cannot be measured, three independent model readings are voted, and code turns the settled judgments into a 1-10 rating.
CONCEPT.audience_note: this spec serves two uses: explaining the VAE to others (read concept_model first) and operating/maintaining it (everything after)
problem: Peter Yuill paints large abstract sumi-ink works (mega-brushes, Chinese papers, ~97x180 cm), a year-long Crucible Year practice of 368+ numbered works T_001..
he wants an accurate, trackable 1-10 rating per work, comparable across the year, to see what improved and how

previous engines (V7/V10/V10C) felt 'only slightly better than a guess'; they rewarded heavy, textured, layered material load, which is Peter's baseline, not his quality: T_323 (Peter 5) scored 9 and T_326 (Peter 6) scored 10
a first V22 attempt decomposed judgment into a 14-step, per-cell evidence cascade; two blind reads of the same paintings disagreed on 30-70% of axes, so finer decomposition did not buy reliability
approach: measure first: deterministic Python on the 16-bit TIFF master measures every property that can be measured (ink masses, edges, overlaps, stroke paths, weight, unpainted voids, movement directions, edge contact) and hands those to the model as facts that outrank its own reading
judge lean: the model answers one categorical question per axis, choosing a rung on a fixed five-rung ladder, writing its observation before its choice and naming what fails the next rung up
buy consistency by ensembling: the same lean call is run three times independently and voted; disagreement is reported as unresolved, never averaged

make rarity structural: the top rung ('master') means the excellent quality held everywhere without exception plus one further property, proven by a complete survey, and it only survives if all three runs independently award it with high confidence; Python checks the survey against the measurements
keep the number out of the model: the model never sees a score; code computes the rating from the settled rungs with weights Peter can read and change
how_it_works: Step 1 (Python, zero model calls): from the TIFF, find ink (darkest 5 of 9 tonal bands), split it into elements, splatter and residue; profile every edge (crisp, soft, broken, bloom-like); find cells where passes overlap and how many tonal bands they hold; trace each stroke's path, width and endpoints; count masses and weight displacement; find held voids (paper with ink on opposite sides) and how crisp their limits are; read the dominant and opposing movement directions; record where ink meets each sheet edge and where weight sits against the sheet's centre, centre lines and edge midpoints
Step 1 output is validated against Peter's eye via colour overlays, never against a model

Step 2 (model): one prompt per painting carries the measured facts in plain cell-named English plus five views of the sheet (the photograph, a greyscale with a red 6x3 grid, a hand-picked close-up crop, an inverted view showing unpainted paper as shape, a low-pass view showing weight); the model names the sheet's parts, then classifies 13 axes
Step 2 (code): validate each run's JSON, cap any rung-4 claim whose survey contradicts a measurement, vote the three runs per axis, apply the master gate, compute the rating
Step 3 (model, later): turns the settled findings into readable critical prose in four sections plus a free response ('NEON'), forbidden to change any finding

axes_plain.A1: Material Control: did the ink's behaviour on this paper stay governed; rare = a material behaviour (a halted bleed, a contained bloom) doing structural work where loss was likeliest
axes_plain.A2: Edge Command: do edge kinds vary with structural role; rare = an edge alone carries a relationship (a crisp shared edge locks ink and void)
axes_plain.A3: Stroke Conviction: do principal strokes read as committed continuous acts; rare = a full-length stroke with visible velocity that stays sound in every phase
axes_plain.B1: Layer Architecture: do overlapping passes stay distinct with consistent depth; rare = the darkest register confined to structural positions
axes_plain.B2: Resolution: did the sheet stop where its structure was complete (no clutter in voids, unresolved ends, filling, retrace); rare = every part costs something if removed
axes_plain.C1: Void: is unpainted paper a shaped, load-bearing part of the structure; rare = void and ink lock at crisp shared junctions and the void reads as a shape in its own right
axes_plain.C2: Equilibrium: how the weight is handled; rare = balance held by opposing movements, not mass alone
axes_plain.C3: Directional Structure: what organises movement; rare = two opposing movements, each spanning a third of the sheet, unified by a shared centre, void or axis
axes_plain.C4: Frame Engagement: how the structure meets the four edges; rare = three or more edges each doing a different named job with the structure placed against the sheet
axes_plain.C5: Load-Bearing Parts: do parts beyond the primary carry load nothing else could; rare = removing a part changes a property of the primary itself
axes_plain.D1: Chance Integration: what the painting did with chance events (bloom, splatter, drip); rare = the event was made to happen there and the passage's structure depends on it
axes_plain.D2: Visual Cadence: where a unit repeats, does the sequence do something; rare = a deliberate break in the sequence that the structure uses
axes_plain.D3: Risk: how difficult was what the sheet attempted, and did it hold; rare = two or more high-difficulty acts hold and the sheet's principal relation depends on both

rung_meaning.0: structural failure (must sit in a structural position or recur)
rung_meaning.2: strong: a named quality clearly achieved, a minority
rung_meaning.3: excellent: the quality in a compound demanding form, uncommon
rung_meaning.4: master: rung 3 held everywhere without exception plus a further property; a handful across a career

CONCEPT.rating: rating = clip(3 + 2 x weighted mean rung, 1, 10) over resolved axes; pre-calibration weights: structural C1-C4 x2, A2 A3 B2 C5 D1 x1, A1 B1 D2 D3 x0.5; an all-competent sheet (every axis rung 1) rates 5; weights will be refit against Peter's own ratings on a 16-work calibration set
what_failed_before: V21.5-derived ladders on a 10-painting run: floor rungs fired on single instances (PHASE_FAILURE 7/10, WORKED_PAST_REPEATEDLY 7/10), top rungs passed easily (5/10), some axes never discriminated (COHERENT 9/10), two axes never produced a value
the model's own read of how many ink masses a sheet has disagreed with itself on 4 of 10 paintings across sessions, whatever facts it was given: gestalt judgments are volatile, so V22 measures them
evidence_so_far: hand-check of six Peter-rated works against the new ladders (not a model run): the structural axes C1-C4 separate Peter's 9s (T_333, T_338, T_317) from his 5s and 6s (T_326, T_323, T_327) the way he did, while material/layer axes A1/B1 do not: layering is his baseline
what his 9s have and his 5s lack: a held, clean, load-bearing void; opposing movements unified; balance carried by direction; structure placed against the sheet's edges

Step 1 overlays checked on T_128, T_313, T_323, T_326, T_328: voids, movements and edge contact read correctly except large voids beyond ~40% of the short side (T_326's arc interior) which are not measured
no calibration model run has been made yet; accuracy is unproven until the 16-work set is run and reported

pipeline.name: deterministic measurement
pipeline.input: TIFF 16-bit master /mnt/c/cortex/images/TIFF 16-BIT/t_NNN.tif (+ 2576px analysis JPEG for field_scale/gesture topology)
pipeline.output: data/measurements/<group>/T_NNN.json, one file per group, overwrite by work_id (deterministic)

groups.segmentation: A: elements (connected ink >= 0.5 cell length, orientation-split by structure tensor), splatter attached to parent elements (per-blob then per-cluster vote), independent residue (individual + populations with width/tone/interval constancy)
groups.boundary_profile: B: per-element per-cell edge segments; trait HARD | SOFT_FEATHERED | BROKEN_RAGGED | UNCERTAIN_BLOOM_FAMILY | UNCLASSIFIED from width/fill_ratio_p10/ring_depth/frag_count; mask_reconstruction_reliable flag
groups.pass_overlap: C: candidate cells (ink density >= 0.3 or >= 2 elements) with density, darkness, tone_std, band_area_fractions (9 bands), n_bands_occupying (bands >= 15% of cell), entropy, coherence, orientation peaks; not a verdict
groups.gesture_profile: D: per element skeleton longest path, width profile, endpoint fill/fragment evidence at radii 50/100/200/300 px, likely_failed (fill@200 <= 0.30, advisory), width_turn events
groups.field_scale: E: num_masses (blur sigma 0.08*short side, threshold band<=4, >=1% area), mass displacement label CENTRED|<compass>_SLIGHT|<compass>_MARKED (<0.05 / >0.15 of half-diagonal), element_groupings
groups.voids: held voids H1..: closing of structural ink (disk r=0.2*short side) AND paper with structural ink before/after along row or column within 2r; per void cells, area_fraction, held_axes, touches_edges, perimeter_by_cell{ink_edge_px, crisp_fraction (Sobel/8 >= 0.06)}, open_perimeter_fraction, marks_inside(+cells)
groups.orientation_field: structure tensor (sigma 0.01*short side) on ~1440px luma with specks painted out by grey closing (25px); axial angles 0-180 (0 horizontal, 90 vertical, CCW, y up); dominant family = histogram peak (36 bins); opposing = peak >= 45 deg away and >= 0.35 of dominant; per-cell angle/strength; extent = share of 6 long-axis positions
groups.frame_contact: per edge N S W E: contact_fraction, runs (fractions along edge), margin_fraction; weight_centre (darkness below paper median tone) and densest_point (blur sigma 0.08) with cell and anchors within 0.05 (sheet centre, centre lines, edge midpoints)

shared.ink: Rec.709 luma quantised to 9 equal bands over 0-65535; ink = band <= 4 (darkest 5 of 9)
shared.grid: landscape 6 cols A-F x 3 rows; portrait 3 cols A-C x 6 rows; cell_at(x,y,w,h)
shared.sheet_view: deterministic/sheet.py: block-mean luma to ~1440px long side; structural_ink = ink minus components < 0.0005 of sheet

Held voids tinted cyan with their ink-facing limit green where crisp and red where not; per-cell movement direction as short lines (orange = dominant family, magenta = opposing, grey = neither); edge contact as yellow bars on the frame; weight centre as a white ring, densest point as a yellow ring.

pipeline/resolve_step2.py.doc: Resolves a painting's finished Step 2 runs: validate, cross-check, vote, gate, rate. Reads data/step2_runs/T_NNN/, writes data/step2_results/T_NNN.json (deterministic from the run files, so re-running overwrites). A missing or unparseable run file counts as an invalid run.

pipeline/step1_coverage.py.doc: Regenerates 16-VAE/v22/STEP1_COVERAGE.md: one row per painting with all eight Step 1 groups measured, linked to its page in the painting archive, plus the paintings that still have a TIFF but no complete Step 1 data. Generated from data/measurements and cortex.db (read-only); never hand-edit the output, re-run this instead.

step2/axes.py.doc: The thirteen v2 axes, their five-rung ladders (index = rung) and the closed vocabularies of the Step 2 output. Single source of truth for the schema, the vote and the rating; the prompt's ladders must match it (checked in test_prompt_matches_registry).

constants.AXES: expr:(Axis('A1', 'Material Control', ('LOST', 'GOVERNED', 'MATERIAL_SHAPES', 'MATERIAL_SHAPES_UNDER_LOAD', 'MATERIAL_MASTERED'), False), Axis('A2', 'Edge Command', ('EDGES_FAIL', 'EDGES_HOLD', 'EDGES_DIFFERENTIATED', 'EDGE_CARRIES', 'EDGE_MASTERY'), False), Axis('A3', 'Stroke Conviction', ('HESITANT', 'SOUND', 'COMMITTED', 'SPEED_WITHOUT_HASTE', 'MASTER_STROKE'), False), Axis('B1', 'Layer Architecture', ('MUDDIED', 'LEGIBLE', 'ORDERED', 'DARK_PLACED', 'DEPTH_MASTERED'), True), Axis('B2', 'Resolution', ('WORKED_PAST', 'RESOLVED', 'CLEAN', 'ECONOMICAL', 'INEVITABLE'), False), Axis('C1', 'Void', ('LEFTOVER', 'SHAPED', 'LOAD_BEARING', 'INTERLOCKED', 'VOID_AS_EQUAL'), True), Axis('C2', 'Equilibrium', ('SLIDING', 'SETTLED', 'COUNTERWEIGHTED', 'HELD_IN_TENSION', 'POISED'), False), Axis('C3', 'Directional Structure', ('SCATTERED', 'SINGLE_MOVEMENT', 'WITH_COUNTER', 'OPPOSED_AND_UNIFIED', 'ORCHESTRATED'), False), Axis('C4', 'Frame Engagement', ('TRAPPED', 'CONTAINED_OR_CONTINUING', 'EDGE_ACTIVE', 'EDGES_COMPOSED', 'FRAME_INEVITABLE'), False), Axis('C5', 'Load-Bearing Parts', ('REDUNDANT', 'SUPPORTING', 'NECESSARY', 'RECIPROCAL', 'INTERDEPENDENT'), True), Axis('D1', 'Chance Integration', ('DISRUPTIVE', 'ACCEPTED', 'INCORPORATED', 'GENERATED', 'EXPLOITED'), True), Axis('D2', 'Visual Cadence', (None, 'REPEATED', 'VARIED_WITH_PURPOSE', 'SYNCOPATED', 'CADENCE_MASTERED'), True), Axis('D3', 'Risk', ('FAILED_RISK', 'WITHIN_REACH', 'RISK_HELD', 'RISK_IS_STRUCTURE', 'MASTER_RISK'), False))
constants.AXIS_BY_KEY: expr:{a.key: a for a in AXES}

step2/calibration.py.doc: Calibration set (spec, seed 20260923) and the report that answers the spec's three accuracy questions: consistency (repeat-run agreement per axis), gut agreement (engine rating vs Peter's p_rating), discriminative power (rank correlation overall and per axis).

step2/crosscheck.py.doc: Checks a rung-4 master_survey against what Step 1 measured. Any contradiction caps that run's value at rung 3 (spec: "One contradiction caps the axis at rung 3"). Measured checks exist for the axes Step 1 reaches directly: C1 (when the survey covers a measured void, every limit cell of it surveyed and crisp), A1 (every overlap cell the facts mark heavy surveyed), C4 (all four edges surveyed). Every axis also fails on a survey entry that itself records an exception.

defs._surveyed_void: The measured void the survey is about: the first (largest) whose limit cells the survey covers at least half of. None when the survey is about a void Step 1 did not measure (the model's V1 need not be H1, and voids wider than ~40% of the short side are not measured).

step2/facts.py.doc: Loads one painting's Step 1 measurements and renders them as the compact, cell-named lines the Step 2 prompt's known_facts block takes. Cells, words and shares only; no pixel coordinates reach the model.

step2/fill.py.doc: Fills the Step 2 template with rendered facts. Raises on a missing fact or a leftover placeholder rather than sending a half-filled prompt.

step2/images.py.doc: The five views Step 2 sends, in the prompt's order, from the live image master (/mnt/c/cortex/images -> C:\AA_CY_IMAGE_MASTER).

step2/rating.py.doc: Deterministic 1-10 rating from resolved axis rungs: clip(intercept + slope * weighted mean rung, 1, 10), over axes that resolved to a rung. NOT_PRESENT, NOT_ESTABLISHED and unresolved axes are excluded from the denominator and listed. Weights live in rating_weights.json, readable and adjustable by Peter; the model never sees them.

step2/schema.py.doc: Builds the JSON Schema every Step 2 run must satisfy, from the axis registry. `python -m step2.schema --write` regenerates schema/step2_output_v2.schema.json; a test keeps the file in sync.

step2/validate.py.doc: Schema validation of one Step 2 run record. Returns readable error strings (empty list = valid); never raises on bad model output.

step2/vote.py.doc: Resolves a painting's ensemble of Step 2 runs into one value per axis.
